answer: Each agent computes a deterministic aggregate over the verifier-named public dataset slice, publishing count and checksum within 30 minutes; the lotus slice holds 50,000 records and the verifier recomputes it from the same slice and compares both. One honest agent runs 1 aggregation on 4 CPU cores for a 150 POA bond; 10 fakes must run 10 aggregations on 40 cores, so compute cost rises 10X. A wrong count or checksum mismatch on the velvet lagoon slice slashes the 150 POA bond and freezes repeat offenders.
